fix: address code review findings (5 issues)

- Hook socket: add semaphore (128 max) + 1s per-connection timeout
  to prevent unbounded task spawning (local DoS vector)
- resolve_symlink: walk read_link chain manually so dangling symlinks
  (stow-managed dotfiles) resolve to the target path instead of
  silently falling back to the symlink itself
- JSONL watcher: single metadata() call per walk_jsonl invocation,
  eliminating TOCTOU race between is_dir check and file_len read
- pixel_painter: replace duplicated EXIT_WINDOW_MS const with import
  from reducer::EXIT_GRACE_WINDOW (single source of truth)
- ascii-agents: remove test-renderer feature from release deps — only
  activated via --features flag in CI and tests

feat(tui): cat state machine + sit/sleep sprites + desk visits

Cat behavior overhaul — 45s cycle with desk visits:
- 0-30%: walk corridor left→right
- 30-40%: walk from corridor to deterministic target desk
- 40-70%: sit (cat_sit) or sleep (cat_sleep with z's) at the desk
- 70-80%: walk back to corridor
- 80-100%: walk corridor right→left

Sleeps (with animated z's) when visiting an idle agent's desk or when
all agents are idle. Sits upright otherwise.

New sprites (4 iterations on walk, 1 on sit/sleep):
- cat_sit.sprite: 6×6 front-facing, ears up, eye, white chest, tail
- cat_sleep.sprite: 6×4 curled up ball with tail wrapped
- cat_walk v4: 8×6 chunky side view with triangular ears, visible
  eye on orange face, white chest patch — reads as "cat" at scale

Added palette key `u` (#3a2010) for cat dark details.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tui): ticker queue persistence + cat teleport + desk overlap

Ticker:
- Replace per-frame ticker rebuild with persistent TickerQueue that
  appends new tool events to the end of a scrolling buffer
- Messages scroll off naturally like a news crawl, new events append
- Buffer capped at 512 chars with oldest trimmed
- Starts with GitHub star promo, tool events accumulate on top

Cat fixes:
- Fix teleport at cycle boundary: corridor walk now goes left→mid
  (directly below target desk) instead of left→right, so the
  transition to desk walk is spatially continuous
- Fix desk overlap: cat sits in front of desk (y = desk.y + DESK_H + 2)
  so y-sort paints it on top, not behind the desk sprite
- All 5 phases have continuous position: corridor→desk→sit→desk→corridor

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(tui): cat roams entire office — desks, pantry, sofas, couch

Cat now picks from all available spots each 40s cycle: home desks,
pantry counter, meeting sofas, lounge couch, corridor center. Walks
directly from previous spot to next (no corridor-only phase). Sleeps
with z's at idle agent desks or when all agents are idle, sits
upright otherwise.

Eliminates the rigid 5-phase corridor-centric cycle. Each cycle is
a simple walk (35%) + rest (65%) between two deterministic spots,
making the cat feel like it actually lives in the office.

feat: crash log with panic hook + terminal restore

On panic: restores terminal (raw mode, alternate screen, mouse

Ensures the terminal is usable after a crash instead of leaving it
in raw mode with invisible cursor.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: TickerQueue char-boundary panic + build.rs stale path + hook semaphore

Critical fixes from code review round 2:

- TickerQueue::drain panicked on multi-byte char boundary (★, ·, →)
  — now uses char_indices().nth() for safe trim (C1)
- TickerQueue::visible used byte length as char skip count causing
  scroll jumps — now uses chars().count() for modulo (C2)
- build.rs pointed to assets/sprites/default/ which no longer exists
  after sprite move — now points to sprites/default/ (C3)
- sprite_format.rs test referenced ../../assets/sprites/default —
  fixed to ../ascii-agents/sprites/default (C4)
- Hook semaphore acquired inside spawn (no back-pressure) — now
  acquired before accept via acquire_owned() (H1)
- TickerQueue used → and · separators (multi-byte) — switched to
  ASCII : and | to minimize future boundary issues (H2)
- Removed unused _now param from TickerQueue::update (M1)

desk count for the current terminal. Keep fetch_max for the per-frame
update (monotone growth prevents cumulative-offset shifts that would

fix(jsonl): unify the first-sight gate — stop the rescan resurrecting ended/stale sessions (#85) (#104)

* fix(jsonl): unify the first-sight gate so the rescan can't resurrect ended/stale sessions

The recency + session_end gate lived ONLY in `initial_seed_walk`; the 250ms
post-startup rescan (and the 60s poll / notify path) read a first-sight file
from offset 0 via `walk_jsonl` with NO gate. When the initial `read_dir` lost
the APFS metadata-propagation race (amplified under heavy parallel-test CPU
load), the missed ended/stale file was read fresh and emitted a phantom
SessionStart — the #85 flake, AND a real resurrect-on-restart product bug (an
abruptly-restarted watcher briefly showed an already-ended session as a live
sprite).

gate (`should_seed_at_eof`: mtime outside the window OR a session_end marker in
the tail → seed the cursor at EOF, no SessionStart), and the initial seed runs
through the same `scan_root` -> `walk_jsonl` path every later scan uses. Deletes
the divergent `initial_seed_root`/`initial_seed_walk` so the two paths can't
disagree again.

Behavior preserved (pinned): a recent live file still emits SessionStart; a
seeded-at-EOF file still revives on the next append (it becomes `known` with
cursor < len). Deterministic unit tests drive `walk_jsonl` directly on
never-seeded ended/stale/live files (no timing race). Stress-verified: 0
failures across 25 runs of the formerly-flaky suite under 8x CPU load.

Fixes #85.

fix(reducer): asymmetric hook-wins dedup — Task self-END can no longer be eaten by its dispatch record (#150) (#154)

* fix(reducer): asymmetric hook-wins dedup — a Task self-END can no longer be eaten by its dispatch record (#150)

The dedup map was event-kind-blind: a hook Task ActivityStart's record
dropped the genuine JSONL ActivityEnd for the same tool_use_id inside
HOOK_WINS_WINDOW. When the PostToolUse hook also dropped (best-effort
shim, documented-real), that JSONL END was the only completion signal —
eating it leaked active_tasks[parent] for the rest of the session: every
later parent hook event suppressed as a subagent leak, and the b1
completion cascade disabled for all future delegations.

Fix: record the hook event's kind in the dedup map VALUE (the End
overwrites its tool's Start entry, exactly as the kind-blind map did)
and drop asymmetrically — an End record suppresses both JSONL kinds (a
lagged JSONL Start replay for an ended tool would falsely re-Activate
and cancel the armed idle debounce), a Start record suppresses only
Starts. Kind-in-the-value (not the key) is load-bearing: it preserves
the End-dominates window that covers a tool's whole lagged JSONL pair —
a symmetric (id, kind, tuid) key would have regressed exactly that path.
Design adversarially checked (3-agent panel; both advocates + risk
auditor converged on the asymmetric matrix).

Behavior unchanged for Starts byte-for-byte; only the End drop narrows.
No-op for Codex (tuids always None on both transports) and Antigravity
(no hook transport). Suppress-before-record (leg 1, #90) is a same-kind
hazard and stays load-bearing — its pin passes unchanged.

* fix(reducer): grace-deferred b1 cascade + conditional stale-gate clear (#151, #152)

#151A: a parallel SECOND Task dispatch arriving via hook is suppressed
as a subagent leak and tracked only via its JSONL copy. If the FIRST
Task's END drained active_tasks while that copy was still in watcher
latency, the immediate b1 cascade evicted the second Task's LIVE
subtree — unrecoverably: exiting_at has no clearer, and after the 4.5s
GC the child's JSONL events no-op forever (its SessionStart is behind
the cursor). The b1 cascade is now deferred by B1_CASCADE_GRACE (2.5s)
via pending_b1_cascades; any Task insert for that parent cancels it
(the suppressed dispatch's JSONL copy is the canceling signal — the
drain's own tool_result write triggers the notify that replays the
backlogged dispatch line, so one FSEvents hop is all the grace covers).
Fire-time emptiness re-check as defense in depth; eviction at both
sweep sites like the sibling maps; SessionEnd and stale-sweep cascades
stay immediate (their signals aren't latency-racing). Sizing anchors on
the const; the 60s-poll double-missed-notify outlier is consciously
residual (documented in #151 and the sharp edges).

#152 (upgraded from hygiene by the design panel's trace): the gate
recorded while Delegating holds the Task's own tuid; the drain path
deliberately skips the main arm, so the entry went stale — and a late
out-of-window JSONL replay of the same END false-matched it via
resolves_wait, flipping a still-pending permission Waiting to Idle. The
drain now clears the gate CONDITIONALLY (only its own tuid): an
unconditional clear would wipe a parallel ordinary tool's legitimate
gate (task_drain_keeps_parallel_ordinary_tool_gate pins this).

Design adversarially checked (4-agent panel: grace-delay vs provisional
tracking vs accept; 3/4 converged on grace-delay — provisional's JSONL
confirmation depends on the same laggy transport it compensates for,
and a suppressed parallel dispatch is hook-indistinguishable from a
nested sub-dispatch, so per-tuid pending state would silently defer
every b1 if CC ever ships nesting).

not-exiting at the drain + exiting after the grace; the leg-1 ordering
pin's no-cascade assert moved to after a grace tick (asserting at the
drain instant would pass under the record-before-suppress mutant —
teeth relocated, not lost); jsonl_task_self_end_drains... ticks past
the grace. New pins: late_jsonl_dispatch_copy_inside_grace_cancels_
premature_cascade (the #151A repro, red on main) and late_jsonl_replay_
of_drained_task_end_does_not_false_resolve_waiting (the #152 repro,

fix: bound the Unix shim's connect phase with the Windows watchdog (#167) (#170)

UnixStream::connect has no timeout knob — a backlog-saturated listener
(wedged daemon accept loop) parks connect() indefinitely, past the
200ms invariant-#5 budget that set_write_timeout only enforces AFTER a
successful connect. Adopt the Windows arm's watchdog verbatim:
Builder::spawn → sleep(200ms) → exit(0); spawn-err → return (thread
exhaustion degrades to a dropped event); the write timeout stays as a
second layer.

Consequences pinned in the same commit:
- send_line's in-process unit tests DELETED on purpose — the watchdog
  hard-exits the process ~200ms after any call, which would kill
  sibling tests under plain cargo test's shared-process runner (the
  same reason the Windows arm never had in-process tests). Coverage
  lives at the child-process level: tests/shim.rs delivery +
  missing-socket + the new stalled-listener twin.
- New stalled_listener_shim_exits_zero_within_watchdog_bound: 160
  parked fillers saturate the backlog; Linux blocks the shim's connect
  (watchdog arm, exercised on CI), macOS refuses fast — both exit 0
  within the bound. Name rides #169's nextest threads-required
  override.
- Latency bounds unified at 1500ms across shim.rs and shim_pipe.rs:
  ~200ms watchdog-bounded child runtime + spawn-jitter margin (the
  jitter term is handled by the #169 serialization, not the bound).
- Invariant #5 text updated (CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md): watchdog on

THE GAP: CC Workflow-tool fleets spawn subagents with NO per-agent Agent
tool_use in the parent transcript, so b1 (Task-drain exit) structurally
can't fire; their transcripts carry no end marker; and the decoder
deliberately narrowed SubagentStart/SubagentStop to Codex. Finished fleet
agents therefore idled until the 10/30-min stale sweeps batch-reaped
them, holding desks and starving the next wave.

WIRE FACTS (captured live, CC v2.1.170; sanitized fixture pinned in
tests/sources/claude/fixtures/hook-payloads.jsonl): SubagentStart carries
the parent's session_id/transcript_path/cwd plus agent_id (BARE hex — no
"agent-" prefix) and agent_type ("general-purpose" | "workflow-subagent");
SubagentStop adds agent_transcript_path (the subagent's own transcript,
incl. the deeper subagents/workflows/wf_*/ nesting) and noise fields we
tolerate but don't consume (last_assistant_message, background_tasks,
effort, permission_mode, session_crons).

- claude_code::decode_cc_hook_custom — SubagentStart → SessionStart for
  the child keyed `agent-<id>` (the transcript-stem id space; tolerates
  an already-prefixed wire id without double-prefixing) with

  SessionEnd keyed on cc_id_from_path(agent_transcript_path) — EXACT
  parity with the JSONL watcher's id deriver — falling back to the
  prefixed wire id when the path is absent. Claim-fully: malformed
  instances Err (log + skip), never fall through or mint phantoms.
- install: CC now registers SubagentStart/SubagentStop alongside the
  existing five events; a re-run over an older install ADDS them

  CC_KNOWN_OMITTED (a registered event vanishing = breaking; a NEW
  upstream event = review ping). Verified live: 30 upstream events, all

test(core): de-flake exit_watch live tests (10s liveness bound + reap-before-assert) (#325)

The coverage (llvm-cov) job intermittently failed
`exit_watch::tests::live::drop_stops_cleanly` with FAIL + LEAK — surfaced
on #322's CI, unrelated to that lockfile bump (passed 1707/1707 locally
and on re-run).

Root cause: these `live::` tests put a 3s wall-clock deadline on real
process / thread machinery. Under llvm-cov instrumentation + full nextest
parallelism on a loaded runner, the watcher thread's post-Drop
kqueue/pidfd wake occasionally isn't scheduled within 3s -> the assert
fires (FAIL). The panic then skips drop_stops_cleanly's trailing
kill_and_reap -> the `sleep 30` child leaks -> nextest LEAK.

Distinct from the #161/#167 shim de-flake (those were pixtuoid-hook
latency tests, given threads-required); exit_watch's live tests arrived
later (#228) and reused the wall-clock-on-real-process pattern without the
mitigation.

Fix (test-only, no production change):
- LIVE_PID_DEADLINE const = 10s, replacing the five 3s deadlines. A
  liveness ceiling, not a latency assertion: a true hang is still failed
  by nextest's 180s slow-timeout, so the wider bound doesn't weaken it.
- drop_stops_cleanly reaps the child BEFORE the assert, so a slow drop can
  never also leak the sleeper.

Drop itself is race-free (kqueue retains the EVFILT_USER trigger — no lost
wakeups), so this is jitter headroom, not masking a real bug. Live tests
10/10 green locally; preflight 1707 green.

`live::*` tests spawn a real child, watch its pid via kqueue/pidfd, and assert

they run isolated and the watcher thread is never starved. NOT a retry (#161's
no-retries stance is preserved); the `ci` profile inherits it; the macOS/Linux

fix(exit-watch): close the Linux self-pipe lost-wakeup that flaked drop_stops_cleanly (#354)

The `coverage` job kept flaking `exit_watch::tests::live::drop_stops_cleanly`
at exactly LIVE_PID_DEADLINE (10.02s) on `main` — including AFTER #353. #353
misdiagnosed it as CPU contention and added a `threads-required = "num-cpus"`
nextest override; that didn't help because the bug is a LOGIC race, not
scheduling.

Root cause (Linux pidfd backend only): a self-pipe lost-wakeup. `Drop` sets
`closed` then writes a wake byte, but the run loop drains the pipe
UNCONDITIONALLY after its post-poll `closed` check. A Drop landing between that
check and the drain has its wake byte eaten, leaving `closed = true` with an
empty pipe — so the thread re-enters poll() and blocks on the still-live watched
child (`sleep 30`) until the 10s test timeout. The clean, repeatable 10.02s
(not variable jitter) is the tell, and it only reproduces on the ubuntu CI
(macOS's EVFILT_USER trigger is consumed by kevent() itself — no separate drain
to eat it).

Fix: re-check `closed` at the TOP of the loop, before blocking in poll(). SeqCst
pairs with Drop's store-before-wake, so a drained byte still leaves the next
load observing `true` — the window is closed by construction. This is a real
production bug too (the watcher thread could leak on shutdown), not just a test
flake.

Also:
- Revert #353's isolation override + its (wrong-cause) doc comment.
- Loop `drop_stops_cleanly` 50× to stress the watch()-then-drop() race so CI
  reliably catches a regression (one unfixed iteration hangs the whole test;
  fixed, all 50 close in ms — 0.53s locally).

Verified: macOS build/clippy/fmt clean, full pixtuoid-core suite green (546).
The Linux block compiles by construction (the added line is identical to the
existing post-poll check in the same cfg block); ubuntu CI is the authority.

  on a code branch with unmet attestation/blocking checks; a `PreToolUse(Bash)`
  hook denies `--no-verify`/`SKIP_PREFLIGHT` git ops and gates `git push`/`gh pr

  substance.

* fix(daemon): PidExited must not resurrect an absent daemon as a phantom mascot

Whole-codebase correctness audit (core-liveness + concurrency-seam, deduped).
`apply_presence` ran `or_insert_with` for EVERY delta before the match, so a
`PidExited` — a DEATH signal synthesized by the exit-watch drain, not decoded
proof of life — minted a fresh UP entry for a daemon that was never seen or was
already TTL-removed. The fresh entry's `current_pid == None` fails the arm's
`current_pid == Some(pid)` guard, leaving it UP: a live idle lobster mascot for
a gateway that is actually dead, until the next ~5-min TTL sweep.

Trigger: OpenClaw connected, gateway idle > presence_ttl_ms (no heartbeat
variant, so a genuinely idle gateway is TTL-removed while alive), then the
still-armed pid is killed → PidExited fires to the connected source with no
entry-existence filter.

Make `PidExited` non-creating: fetch via `get_mut` and no-op if absent, matching
`sweep_presence_ttl`'s deliberate non-creating design. Every other (proof-of-
life) delta still (re)creates UP. Match stays exhaustive (no unreachable!).

* fix(scene): treat empty XDG_CONFIG_HOME as unset for the sprite-pack dir

Whole-codebase correctness audit (scene-theme-misc, cross-platform lens).
`xdg_pack_dir` read XDG_CONFIG_HOME with `var_os` and only fell back to
`<home>/.config` on ABSENT (None). A SET-but-EMPTY value (common: a script does
`export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$UNSET`) is `Some("")`, so the fallback was skipped and
`base` became an empty PathBuf → `pixtuoid/sprites` resolved RELATIVE to the
process CWD. The loader would then probe `./pixtuoid/sprites/pack.toml`: if such
a dir exists under (or is planted in) the launch directory it silently loads
that untrusted pack, while the user's real ~/.config pack is ignored.

The XDG basedir spec (and the dirs crate) mandate empty == unset. Extract a pure
`xdg_config_base(env_value, home)` that filters an empty value before mapping, so
it falls through to the default — mirroring the repo's own io::nonempty_env
convention. Pure (env value passed in) → unit-testable without mutating process
env.

falls_back_to_home_when_absent, is_none_without_xdg_or_home}. 10 embedded_pack

* fix(security): strip Unicode bidi controls (Trojan-Source) from terminal output

Whole-codebase security audit (security-sweep). `strip_control_chars` — the one
chokepoint for untrusted strings reaching a terminal sink (headless summary,
doctor stdout, Sources panel; agent labels, sampled CLI output, config paths,
pack.name/version) — filtered only `char::is_control()`, i.e. category Cc
(C0/C1). The Unicode Bidi_Control characters (RLO/LRO/PDF, the isolates, LRM/RLM/
ALM) are category Cf, so they slipped through — yet they REORDER displayed text
in a terminal (the "Trojan Source" class, CVE-2021-42574), letting an untrusted
label render differently from its underlying bytes (e.g. "exe.gpj" shown for
"gpj.exe").

fix(hook): harden the /tmp socket rendezvous into a per-user 0700 dir (#493)

* fix(hook): harden the /tmp socket rendezvous into a per-user 0700 dir

The no-XDG fallback bound the hook socket at a FLAT, predictable
`/tmp/pixtuoid-{uid}.sock`. A co-located other user could pre-create/lock
`{sock}.lock` there and silently disable the whole hook plane (the daemon
degrades to transcript-only on SocketBusy), or park a listener to intercept
the payload (cwd, tool names). #485.

Move the fallback into a per-user SUBDIR `/tmp/pixtuoid-{uid}/pixtuoid.sock`:
- Daemon (`hook::unix::bind`) creates `/tmp/pixtuoid-{uid}/` with a TOCTOU-safe
  `mkdir(0700)`; on EEXIST it `lstat`-validates a real dir, owned by us, with no
  group/other bits — a pre-squatted dir/file/symlink fails the bind LOUDLY
  instead of silently degrading. `/tmp`'s sticky bit stops another uid swapping
  our dir once it exists. No-op for the XDG / explicit-`PIXTUOID_SOCKET` parents.
- Shim (`transport::send_line`) lstat-validates that owned dir before connecting
  and drops the event if it's hostile — so it can't be tricked into piping the
  payload into another user's listener parked under a world-accessible dir. An
  absent dir is NOT hostile (the connect just fails fast). One non-blocking
  lstat, scoped to the fallback (XDG/override untouched).

Path change is parity-pinned across shim + daemon (socket_path_parity.rs branch
3 now asserts the subdir literal). Dogfooded live: the headless daemon creates
`/tmp/pixtuoid-{uid}/` as `drwx------` and the shim (no env) delivers a
`gateway_start` → `daemons=[openclaw:idle]`. SECURITY.md updated. Existing flat
`/tmp/pixtuoid-{uid}.sock` residue from older versions is harmlessly orphaned.

Closes #485.

path, so whatever socket we connected to — legit daemon or a raced squatter —

fix(hook): close #495 — Windows named-pipe server-identity check (#497)

* fix(hook): close #495 — Windows named-pipe server-identity check

The #485 read-side leak defense was Unix-only: the Windows shim wrote the hook
payload to whatever pipe answered `\\.\pipe\pixtuoid-{USERNAME}`, so a co-located
user who pre-squatted that (machine-global, predictable) name — making our
daemon's create fail → SocketBusy → silent transcript-only degrade — received
the cwd + tool names + tool_args. An N-1-of-N gap the whole-codebase audit caught
in my own #485 work.

`transport::send_line` (Windows) now verifies the pipe SERVER runs as our user
before writing: `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` → `OpenProcess` →
`OpenProcessToken` → `GetTokenInformation(TokenUser)` → `EqualSid` vs our own
token user. Fail-CLOSED on any FFI failure (drop, never panic — invariant #5);
scoped to our default pipe name (`paths::default_windows_pipe_name`, factored out
of `default_socket_path`) so an explicit `PIXTUOID_SOCKET` pipe stays the user's
trust decision — parity with the Unix `owned_tmp_socket_dir` scoping.

This required windows-sys on the shim (the one crate that was Win32-dep-free) —
but core+binary already depend on it, and verified decls beat hand-FFI in the
never-panic shim; SAME major pinned so the bindings don't double-compile. While
there: the hand-hardcoded `231` → `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY`, and core's `Some(5)` →
`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` (free — Win32_Foundation already imported). New windows-only
teeth test (`server_is_us` on a self-hosted pipe → us). SECURITY.md updated.

(The `install/io.rs` "os error 32" is a comment, not a numeric compare — left as-is.)

Closes #495.

* fix(install): O_NOFOLLOW + O_EXCL on the atomic-write .tmp create

The config write deliberately follows the symlink at the RESOLVED target (stow,
invariant #4), but the `.tmp` beside it was created with a bare O_CREAT|O_TRUNC:

fresh inode); a legit stale .tmp from a crashed run is reclaimed once
(remove_file unlinks the entry itself, never following a symlink). The final
rename onto the resolved target is unchanged, so the through-symlink write still
works. Windows keeps its create+rename-retry path.

fix(site): play the office ♩ audio through iOS silent mode (audioSession=playback) (#665)

* fix(site): play the office ♩ audio through iOS silent mode (audioSession=playback)

On iOS Safari, WebAudio (AudioContext) routes to the ambient channel by
default, so the hardware Ring/Silent switch — very commonly left ON — mutes
it. A visitor who deliberately taps ♩ (an explicit opt-in) then hears nothing,
which reads as broken.

Set `navigator.audioSession.type = 'playback'` at the moment audio is enabled
(before constructing the AudioContext), routing WebAudio to the media channel
so the opt-in plays even on silent — the same reason a <video> plays with the
silent switch on. Feature-guarded (`'audioSession' in navigator`), so it's a
pure iOS enhancement that no-ops on every other browser.

Accepted trade-off (documented in site/CLAUDE.md): 'playback' is the only web
AudioSession category that bypasses the switch and is non-mixing, so it can
pause other apps' audio when ♩ is tapped — acceptable since ♩ is a deliberate
gesture.

The API is Safari-only and the silent-switch behavior is device-only, so CI
can't exercise it; the smoke test mocks navigator.audioSession to pin the
WIRING (type becomes 'playback' on ♩ enable), verified RED without the line.
Real device verification: open the live site on an iPhone with the Ring/Silent
switch ON, tap ♩, confirm sound.

refactor(core): give the #223 probe ladder one owner (ProbeLadder, a pure failure-detector) (#684)

* refactor(core): give the #223 probe ladder one owner (ProbeLadder, a pure failure-detector)

Deferred arch-deepening candidate #2. The probe ladder's DERIVED liveness state
was scattered: `NegativeVouch` owned the vouch hysteresis, but the `pid → ids`
bindings were a bare `ScanState` map with THREE writers (the rebind loop, the
vouch's confirm-unbind via a `&mut` param, and the exit_rx arm poking
`scan_state.pid_bindings.remove`), and the `forget`↔`unbind` inverse was a prose
contract split across a free fn + a method.

Concentrate it into one `ProbeLadder` owner, designed as a **functional core /
imperative shell** (the searched best practice) so the reorg is byte-identical
in the highest-blast-radius subsystem:

- `ProbeLadder::fold(snap, now) -> ProbeOutcome { exits, newly_watched }` is
  PURE — it advances the miss windows + pid bindings and RETURNS the effects
  (confirmed-exit ids to emit + newly-seen pids to watch). It never touches
  `ctx`/`tx`/the exit watch. `now` is a parameter, so it is a unit-testable
  snapshot→exits state machine with synthetic time and zero mocks.
- The shell (`refresh_probe_snapshot`) applies the outcome in the pre-owner
  order — emit BEFORE registering the new pids — so the `AgentEvent` stream on
  the channel is byte-identical (`exit_watch.watch` sends nothing synchronously,
  and each just-confirmed id is absent from `snap.pid_of`, so the watch loop
  never touches it).
- `pid_died(pid) -> Vec<Id>` replaces the exit_rx arm's direct map poke +
  per-id forget. `forget`/`unbind` are now private methods one owner keeps in
  lockstep.

Behavior-preserving — PROVEN by the 10 black-box shell tests in
tests/watcher/liveness.rs (negative vouch, instant exit, rebind migration,
probe failure/panic — all green), per the empirical-verify rule for a
timing/interaction claim in liveness. The two white-box unit tests that drove
the internal map are replaced by 5 pure-ladder tests exercising the new
interface (the deepening's payoff: the interface IS the test surface).

The detection MECHANISM is untouched and already best-practice (pidfd/kqueue
NOTE_EXIT + start-time recycle check + hysteresis); this only gives its
scattered STATE an owner.

feat(web,site): Web Worker synthesis — the ♩ click becomes upload-only (#709)

* feat(web,site): synthesize the take in a Web Worker — the click is upload-only

The remaining path to a near-instant click (the main-thread idle pump
was reverted in the last PR after CI caught it starving clicks on slow
hardware): move synthesis OFF the main thread entirely.

- SynthTake (new wasm export): the worker-side synthesizer. The prewarm
  worker instantiates its OWN wasm module at page idle, selects the same
  day/night + weather track the office would, pumps the whole warmup —
  blocking is fine there — and transfers the buffers back.
- Adoption (audio.rs) + Office::audio_adopt_begin/_oneshot/_loop/_finish:
  the handoff copies the transferred pieces into the page driver one
  small memcpy per timeout tick. The key insight is that the engine tick
  never touches sample data, so an adopted driver is state-identical to
  a locally-warmed one — upload, tick, and the chunked swap downstream
  never know the difference. Every push validates order and bounds, and
  finish validates completeness against the bank consts, so a torn
  handoff (worker died mid-stream) falls back cleanly.
- audio-worker.js (public/, knip-ignored): one message in, one out with
  transferables, then self-close so the worker wasm memory is reclaimed.
- OfficeBackdrop: spawn at requestIdleCallback (timer fallback), settle
  states idle/running/adopted/failed. First ready wins: a click during
  the prewarm DEFERS to settle instead of racing a second driver, and
  adopt_finish refuses to stomp a click-warmed one. Reduced-motion skips
  the prewarm (the low-power stance); the chunked click-time pump stays
  as the fallback for every failure shape.
- e2e: the adopted path pins click→ready under 2.5s (the synthesis path
  it replaces measures seconds); the dead-worker fallback pins that the
  worker is an accelerator, never a dependency. Rust: byte-for-byte
  adoption round-trip, torn-handoff refusals, first-ready-wins, and the
  worker/main determinism the handoff rides on.

Closes #705

PINNED compositing layer (translateZ(0), the Safari hover-jitter fix)
with padding 0, so row 1's 1px chip border sat on the layer's exact top

topmost device-pixel row. Interior rows can't be hit, and headless
Chromium (different rasterizer) doesn't reproduce it — verified with a
pixel probe + rendered crop at iPhone metrics (no geometric clip, no
overlay, opaque chips: the only survivor is the layer raster boundary).

Fix: move 2px of the strip's top margin INSIDE the layer as padding-top
(net geometry identical — margin compensated with calc), so the raster
edge crops padding, never the border.

fix(ci): capture the formula-test output instead of piping into grep -q

packaging-build went red on macos-14 and green on ubuntu-latest. The cause
was the oracle, not the binary: `pixtuoid man | grep -q '^\.TH'` matches on
the FIRST line of roff, so grep -q exits immediately and the still-writing
producer takes EPIPE — with pipefail on, that fails the step.

    pixtuoid 0.16.0
    Error: Broken pipe (os error 32)
       2: pixtuoid::main

Whether it fires is a race against the pipe buffer: Linux's 64K absorbs the
remaining output, macOS's does not. That is a FLAKY assertion — the mirror of
the false-green this job exists to prevent, and just as untrustworthy.

Capture each command to a file, then grep the files. The race disappears, and
`set -e` now checks each binary's OWN exit status instead of grep's.

fix(scripts): openclaw-e2e mid-attach step tested a state it never reached (closes #725) (#737)

* fix(scripts): openclaw-e2e mid-attach step tested a state it never reached

The #318 mid-attach step asserted the daemon was "up with current_pid=None",
then killed a pid and expected an instant abrupt-down. It failed on the very
first execution (once the script was wired into `just openclaw-e2e`).

The premise was false. `PidSeen` adoption is None-ONLY (apply_presence, by
design — GatewayUp owns restart-rebinds and PidSeen must never clobber a live
pid), and the shim stamps `_pid=getppid()` onto every event lacking one. So the
`gateway_start` at step [5] already armed current_pid to the shim's parent;
step [10]'s session_start hit a Some and adopted nothing; killing its pid was a
no-op and the mascot correctly stayed idle. The product was right the whole
time — `#318` works — and the script asserted a precondition it defeated three
steps earlier.

Drive the scenario #318 actually models (the same path openclaw.rs documents):
a reconnect after an abrupt down. `gateway_stop` takes the mascot Down, which
clears current_pid via enter_down; the reconnect is then learned only from a
plain _pid-carrying event, and PidSeen re-adopts because current_pid is None.
The explicit _pid is kept by the shim (an inbound value wins over getppid), so
it is the real live pid.

Verified both ways rather than by reading:
- corrected script: all 12 steps PASS, timeline ends idle -> down (reconnect) ->
  down (abrupt kill off the re-adopted pid);
- mutation: disabling PidSeen adoption in the product reds it at exactly
  `down-abrupt`, so the step now genuinely proves #318 instead of passing
  vacuously — it could not catch a regression before (the issue's own concern).

Closes #725.

made `audio` default: rodio → cpal → alsa-sys, whose build script panics when

this workflow installed it in zero. v0.15.0 predates the audio feature, so the
first tag after #633 is the first to hit it — in the one gate that only ever
runs when it is too late to iterate.

**A tester tag could have auto-bumped homebrew-core from an unreviewed commit.**
Their autobump reads `git ls-remote --tags` and filters pre-releases by keyword
(alpha beta bpo dev experimental prerelease preview rc). `win` is not on that
list, so `v0.16.0-win.1` — a tag this workflow deliberately exempts from the
tag-must-be-on-main check, precisely so it can sit on unmerged code — parses as
a version above the released one and is eligible for a bottle on six platforms.
`-rc` was safe only because its spelling happens to contain a filtered word.

Rename the Windows tester channel `-win.N` → `-winrc.N` and record the
constraint where the exemption is granted, so the next reader does not treat
the name as cosmetic. This is the half we can fix unilaterally; the formula

The prior commit renamed the Windows tester channel `-win.N` → `-winrc.N` so
its suffix would contain `rc`, a word on Homebrew's pre-release keyword filter,
to stop an autobump from picking up an unreviewed tester tag.

That was an invented workaround, not the standard practice. Homebrew's
documented mechanism for excluding pre-release tags is a `livecheck` block on
the FORMULA with a regex that matches only dotted-numeric versions
(`/^v?(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)$/i`) — which excludes EVERY suffix, not just the ones
that happen to contain a filter keyword. The keyword list is Homebrew's
internal fallback, not a contract for upstreams to name their tags against; a
rename here rests on an implementation detail and leaves the next new channel
name (or a typo) able to reopen the exact gap.

The correct fix already existed in #731 (the livecheck regex). Renaming our tag
channel was redundant at best and misleading at worst. Revert it; keep the
ALSA-headers step from the same commit, which is unrelated and sound.

This PR now closes ONE gap (the release check job's missing ALSA headers). The
pre-release/autobump concern is left entirely to #731, where it belongs.

fix(audio): stop the device on quit — RAII teardown, joined off-thread (#746)

Quitting pixtuoid left the rodio/cpal output stream playing until a
`sudo killall coreaudiod` — the device thread was detached, so its
`RodioSink` Drop (the OS device close) lost the race with process exit.

`AudioController` now OWNS the device thread's whole lifecycle: it boot-spawns
in `new` (iff a persisted unmute wants sound) and tears down in `impl Drop`,
which closes the channel and JOINS the thread (bounded by `SHUTDOWN_JOIN_TIMEOUT`
so a hung CoreAudio close can't hang the exit). Because each painter builds the
controller AFTER its fallible `?` boot steps, no device thread ever predates its
Drop-owner, so Drop alone covers every exit path (q / Ctrl-C / terminate / error)
with no hand-wired shutdown. cpal's `Stream` is `!Send`, so the device stays on
its build thread and the join is off-thread.

Device open goes through rodio's `open_default_sink` (keeping its full
device/config fallback) with rodio's `tracing` feature enabled, so mid-session
stream errors, the device-list failure, and the drop log route to `tracing`
instead of an `eprintln!` that would corrupt the TUI altscreen.

Reviewed across three lenses (correctness / concurrency-lifecycle / design-test)
plus the online bot at head (Findings: 0). Regression tests pin both halves of
the RAII guarantee device-free (a muted boot spawns nothing; an unmuted boot's
thread is provably joined on drop), negative-controlled.

fix(ci): stop Dependabot rewriting floating action majors into stale pins (#791)

#786 proposed `@v1` -> v1.0.178 and `@v4` -> v4.37.1. Both are DOWNGRADES: at the
time `@v1` resolved to v1.0.183 and `@v4` to v4.37.3. The floating major tags do

of memory. Vulnerable <= 5.0.7, patched in 5.0.8. The top-level copy is consumed

count is ONE root cause with no local fix: a second copy sits at

extension. Tried: `npm audit` reported 0 vulnerabilities while the code died

than the advisory, so the override is not taken.

fix(openclaw): render each gateway as its own mascot (#787)

Daemon presence is now keyed per INSTANCE, not per source, so N OpenClaw
gateways render N independent lobsters instead of collapsing into one.

- Identity is the resolved gateway PORT — never the profile, pid, or session.
  A profile hosts N concurrent gateways (verified live), so profile cannot tell
  two apart; the port can. The plugin stamps `gatewayPort` on every forwarded
  hook, and a port-less envelope (a stale installed plugin) falls back to one
  legacy instance plus a drift breadcrumb rather than vanishing the mascot.
- `SceneState::daemons` re-keyed by `(source, DaemonInstanceId)`; presence rides
  its own sibling channel as `PresenceMsg { key: DaemonInstanceKey, delta }`, so
  it never enters the `AgentId`-pure `Reducer::apply` (invariant #2).
- Mascot destinations are drawn from the WHOLE walkable floor. The curated
  per-furniture spot list WAS the crowding: it held 3-25 points by terminal size
  and the idle set was structurally 5, so N creatures collided by pigeonhole.
  Measured through the production path (1080 frames, four idle gateways):
  85% of frames crowded before, 42% after — while deleting ~370 lines of
  offset/fallback/claim machinery. Spread, not offset, is the mechanism.
- Entering `Down` anchors the walk-out clock inside `enter_down(now)`, so an
  abrupt death (SIGKILL, no stop hook) plays the elevator walk-out instead of
  vanishing — `last_seen` is a must-set-on-down field at all four down sites.
- Per-run TTL via `in_flight_runs` (a dropped `agent_end` self-heals instead of
  latching Busy), and `Degraded` is gated on an explicit `errored` flag.
- Three e2e tiers, each with a justfile recipe so none can rot unseen:
  `openclaw-e2e` (hermetic, free), `openclaw-multi-e2e` (N real gateways, free),
  `openclaw-backend-e2e` (real gateway + one billed model turn).

fix(site): drive the hero reveal roll by painted frames, not the clock (#794)

On a first visit the hero office reveal froze on a half-drawn frame for ~1.4s and
then snapped to the settled office — the roll was never seen.

Root cause is Safari's own tab-snapshot IPC blocking the page's main thread,
captured with `sample` on both of its processes (Safari 27):

  web process   WebPage::TakeSnapshot -> RemoteImageBufferProxy::flushDrawingContext()
                -> IPC::Semaphore::waitFor -> semaphore_timedwait_trap
  GPU process   RemoteImageBufferSet::endPrepareForDisplay
                -> CA::CG::ContextDelegate::operation_ -> dispatch_sync -> kevent_id

Neither side computes — the GPU process's main thread is 2933/2935 samples idle
and all 28 render-backend threads are parked. It is a CoreAnimation
queue-ownership wait, which is why the duration is near-constant and why no JS
callback in the profile exceeded ~4ms. It co-occurs with the first live office
frame, the same moment the splash's Level-2 gate lifts on.

The stall cannot be prevented; what it must not do is eat the reveal. `rt` was a
wall-clock ramp that kept advancing while nothing painted, so the roll now
accumulates from PAINTED frames: a hitch contributes one clamped step and the
roll pauses through it instead of being skipped. The start waits for frames to
flow (bounded, so a slow device still gets its office), which also defers
`is-live`, `pix:onair` and the sound toggle until the office can actually run.

The four reveal fields live in one object because they share a lifecycle — the
reduced-motion de-live must rewind all of them or the un-reduce snaps.
`REVEAL_MAX_STEP_MS` derives from `FRAME_MS` so the pair cannot drift into
silently disabling the readiness gate.

Verified in real Safari over 24 alternating loads: with a ~1.4s stall inside the
roll, pre-fix wall-clock 1644ms (animation eaten) vs fixed 2971ms (paused, then
played in full); unstalled rolls unchanged. Reveal watched frame-by-frame clean
and under two verified stall placements; 6/6 loads settled, zero console errors.

Three e2e pins added (stall survival, slow-device fallback, un-reduce replay),
each negative-controlled by mutating the source and rebuilding — mutating dist
breaks the inline script's CSP hash and proves nothing. Sharp edge recorded in
site/CLAUDE.md.

fix(site): docs callout invisible in the default day theme, +5 a11y/link defects (#805)

* fix(site): reclaim callout body ink from the .prose cascade

A markdown callout is a `--screen` terminal window dropped inside `.prose`,
so its ink must come from the chip palette. But `.prose p, .prose li
{color: var(--fg)}` matches those elements DIRECTLY, and a direct match
always beats the `--chip-ink` the `.callout__body` blockquote hands DOWN —
inheritance loses to any match, regardless of specificity. The sibling
`.docs :global(.callout__body a)` / `... code)` overrides exist for exactly
that reason; `p`/`li` (and the `strong`/`em` that inherit through them) were
missed, so the DEFAULT day theme rendered every callout as `--fg` #241c14 on
`--screen` #0e0d0c — measured 1.16:1 against a 4.5:1 AA floor, on all three
doc pages that carry a callout (/architecture, /contributing,
/knowledge-base). Night and dracula were incidentally fine: their `--fg` is
light.

Reclaimed at `.docs :global(.callout__body p/li)` (0,2,1), which beats
`.prose p` (0,1,1) by WEIGHT, not source order — the same lift the a/code
rules and the `.prose table th code` guard already use. `color: inherit`
rather than a second `var(--chip-ink)` so the window keeps ONE ink
definition.

Measured on the compiled build via getComputedStyle across day/night/
dracula: p/strong/em 1.16:1 -> 12.58:1, code 14.37:1, a 15.94:1.

The new smoke sweep is the pin: it walks every text-bearing tag markdown can
put in a callout (p, li, strong, em, a, code), on every doc route off the
rendered sidebar, in all three themes — so the next `.prose` colour rule
can't silently re-darken the window, and a docs tree that stopped emitting
callouts fails the vacuity guard instead of passing empty.

* fix(site): make the colour-contrast assertion deterministic, not a coin flip

f4793352 added `"color-contrast": ["error", { "minScore": 1 }]` and left two
sources of nondeterminism under it, either of which makes the gate report
something other than what it claims to.

Aggregation. LHCI's `getStandardAssertionResults` defaults `aggregationMethod`
to `optimistic` (read in @lhci/utils/src/assertions.js, not recalled), and its
`getValueForAggregationMethod` only takes `Math.min` for a `min*` assertion
when the method is `pessimistic`. So a bare `minScore` over `numberOfRuns: 3`
takes `Math.max` — and `color-contrast` is a binary 0/1 axe audit, so ONE clean
run of three greened a total failure. Every other numeric gate in this file
already names `median` or `pessimistic`; this was the only bare one. Now
`pessimistic`: all three runs must clear a contract audit.

Theme. `Base.astro`'s init falls back to night off the 7/19 wall clock and
headless Chrome reports light for `prefers-color-scheme`, so an unqualified
collect URL audits whichever palette the runner's clock happens to hold —
roughly half the runs each way. That was survivable while the only assertion
was a category BUDGET with slack; under a hard per-audit assertion it makes CI
a coin flip on the palette, and a red that reproduces only between 07:00 and
19:00. The six collect URLs now carry `?theme=day` — the documented
`Base.astro` override, ahead of saved choice / clock / system — pinning ONE
palette: the default one, and the one whose light ground the --screen chip inks
are hardest on. Run count is unchanged; doubling the list to audit night here
would only duplicate what smoke.spec.ts already drives explicitly across
day/night/dracula, so the docs now state the division of labour instead:
Lighthouse is the rendered-DOM axe backstop on the pinned theme, the e2e sweeps

* fix(scene): light the weather glass veils with the emitter, not a constant

`skyline_haze` and the Fog/Overcast/Smog `wash_glass` arms were absolute
daylight greys blended over an already-time-lerped `sky_row` with no time
input, so the veil FLIPPED from darkening to brightening after dusk and the

colour), and folding them in would darken a stormy noon veil twice. The floor
is the city-light scatter that keeps fog reading as fog after dark.

`time_of_day_look().darkness` — the interior illuminance — and is structurally
blind to anything the painter lays on the glass afterwards. Three pins: per
weather noon > midnight; no midnight pane out-shines the clear solar-noon
pane; and the counter-pin that fog still glows over the midnight sky, so a
veil scaled to zero can't pass. Fog@noon is unchanged (emitter_lum ~1 at the
apex); fog@midnight drops 152.3 -> 74.1 against a 47.9 clear night.

* fix(watcher): stop a probe-vouched ENDED transcript replaying every scan pass

The first-sight gate's probe bypass skipped the terminator tail-scan as well
as the recency check. Its stated precondition — "NEITHER probe user persists
a structural end marker today" — went stale: the probe roster is now four
(claude_code, codex, grok, omp) and both new members ship a real structural
end-checker (`grok_session_ended`, `omp_session_ended`). So a vouched ENDED
transcript at or below MAX_PENDING_BYTES was registered and fully replayed —
SessionStart + Rename + every historical tool event — and, because the
decoded terminator REMOVED the `seen` claim, `revouch_gated_files` reset the
cursor to 0 and the same thing happened again on the next pass, for as long
as the vouch lasted (unbounded for omp's fd vouch, ~150s for grok's leader
vouch). At desk capacity the phantom can displace a real agent.

Three changes, each pinned red-first:

- `should_seed_at_eof` takes the probe verdict and exempts only the RECENCY
  half. A structural end marker is the source's own first-hand report; a
  liveness vouch is an mtime-independent proxy and must not outrank it. This
  is the call the oversized arm already makes with its unconditional
  `ended_in_skip`.
- `revouch_gated_files` re-runs the same terminator check before resetting a
  cursor, so the sweep cannot undo the park once per scan pass. Placed after
  `probe_admits` so the bounded tail read costs only vouched candidates.
- The decoded-terminator un-claim RELEASES the claim (`seen` -> `false`)
  instead of removing it — the #246 idiom its two sibling un-claim sites
  already use, and which `released_claim_is_not_revouched_into_a_full_replay`
  spells out as the reason. `emit_first_sight` treats `Some(false)` like an
  absent entry, so the documented revive-on-append is byte-identical.

`probe_live_oversized_ended_first_sight_stays_unregistered` now asserts the
park rather than the oversized branch's SessionEnd: a vouched ENDED file no
longer reaches that branch at first sight, and the emission was a reducer
no-op for the unknown id it declined to register. The KNOWN-file

* fix(scope): stop cascade_exit pruning its BFS at an already-exiting node

The child collection filtered on `exiting_at.is_none()`, which treats "already
exiting" as "subtree already handled". That only holds if the subtree was fully
populated at the earlier cascade: a descendant registered under an intermediate
node AFTER that node started exiting was never enqueued, so its own subtree was
never visited and it escaped every subsequent cascade — surviving with a
dangling parent_id and its own 30-min idle timer.

That contradicts scope.rs's one stated invariant (a subagent's lifetime is
contained in its parent's), the fn's own promise to "mark every not-yet-exiting
descendant", and `sweep_exited`'s "in practice cascade_exit reaps the subtree
alongside the parent".

Traversal and stamp are now separate concerns: every child is enqueued
(`visited` alone bounds the walk) and the stamp goes through the write-once
`fsm::mark_exiting` — the same call the root branch already makes. Moving the
stamp is NOT optional: the raw `slot.exiting_at = Some(now)` was only safe
BECAUSE of the filter, so dropping the filter alone would re-stamp an exiting
node on every ancestor cascade, resetting its walkout animation and pushing its
GC out by another EXIT_GRACE_WINDOW each time. The new test asserts the
already-exiting node keeps its ORIGINAL timestamp, and
reducer::lifecycle::reconcile_connected_is_idempotent_on_already_exiting still
passes.

Reachability caveat, recorded honestly: production trees are depth-2 today (CC
flattens subagent paths back to the parent uuid; Codex/copilot subagents are
flat), so this exact depth-3 shape needs a future nesting source — but the
suite already pins stale_sweep_cascades_to_grandchildren, so depth-3 is in
scope by its own definition, and the fix also corrects the doc comment that
described the prune as idempotency.

carries the effective token per invocation, which keeps the two halves reading

step OR on its job reaches green without auditing anything, which retires the
audits exactly as completely as deleting the step, so all four positions are
guards. Each of the four was negative-controlled by deletion; each kills a test.

continue-on-error EXIT=1, and deleting the env block still EXIT=1.

(1) `activate_os` spawned `swaymsg`/`hyprctl` with `Command::status()`, whose

ratatui's diff-based redraw leaves it there until those cells change — and
the child also shares the raw-mode stdin the TUI polls for keystrokes. The
failure path is the common one, given focus's documented misses: `swaymsg`
prints a diagnostic for an unmatched `[pid=N]`. This was the only
full-inherit spawn in the binary (`tree_lists_pid` and `focus::macos` use

already treats the identical class as a bug to fix — audio/sink.rs:112
silences ALSA's stderr for exactly this reason. Both arms now route through
one `run_detached` helper so a third compositor cannot be added un-nulled.

(2) `detect_channel` and `doctor::activation_backend` keyed on bare
`var_os(..).is_some()`. An exported-but-blank `SWAYSOCK` — routinely left by
systemd user units and non-forwarded ssh sessions — therefore read as "sway
is running", routing BOTH the `focusable` probe and the activation to

a permanent silent no-op; the doctor twin printed the Wayland ✗ verdict at a
user whose EWMH channel works. These four were the only env reads in the
binary skipping `install::io::nonempty` ("keep new env reads on this helper
so the workspace has one semantics"). Both sites now use it.

* fix(crash): restore the terminal on stdout, the stream that entered the alt screen

The panic hook wrote `DisableMouseCapture` + `LeaveAlternateScreen` to
STDERR while every other site in the terminal-mode state machine drives
stdout: `setup_terminal` does `execute!(stdout(), EnterAlternateScreen,

`teardown_terminal` writes through `Terminal<CrosstermBackend<Stdout>>`.

These are ANSI sequences delivered to whatever writer `execute!` is handed,

eprintlns its truecolor and config warnings — they went into the redirect.

worked (crossterm resolves its own /dev/tty fd), so raw mode came back while
the alternate screen and mouse reporting did not, leaving the shell prompt
drawn on the alt screen emitting escape bytes on mouse motion. `reset`
required, and the crash message the user needed went to the redirect too.

The restore moves into `restore_terminal(w)` and the hook hands it stdout.
The human-readable report deliberately stays on stderr.

Teeth are on the STREAM, not just the bytes: the hook is process-global and
writes to a real fd, so the new test re-execs the test binary with a child
marker, lets a real panic fire the hook, and reads the two pipes apart —
verified red against the old stderr writer. Unix-only, since on Windows
`execute!` falls back to WinAPI console calls for a non-VT writer, which is
also not the redirection case the defect describes.

`default_hook_binary` consulted PATH before the exe-sibling, while the helper
directly below it states the opposite rule ("exec-form spawning needs the real
PE name; PATHEXT is a shell behavior we must not rely on") and the Windows
design record prescribes sibling-then-`which`. `which` v8 IS PATHEXT-aware, so

extensionless sh script in the global bin dir, while npm/generate.mjs copies

PATH hit is filtered through `path_hit_is_native` and resolution falls through
to the sibling. The wanted extension is a PARAMETER fed
`std::env::consts::EXE_EXTENSION`, so both platforms' truth tables are tested

(empty extension) and never applies to `PIXTUOID_HOOK`.

runtime leg relies on the CI cross-lint plus the platform-parameterised test.

said the rename "REPLACES `p` rather than following a symlink planted at it",
but `write_config_atomic` resolves through symlinks by design (invariant #4;
its own doc says so, and `write_config_atomic_through_symlink_preserves_link`
pins it). Only the `.tmp` is O_NOFOLLOW-hardened. Comment-only — the behavior
is deliberate and already test-pinned.

The event loop ran `floor_capacity` for all MAX_FLOORS floors on EVERY frame
to read ten desk counts. Each call is a full `Layout::compute_with_seed` —
walkable-mask stamp plus coarse BFS, quadratic in buffer area — and everything
but `home_desks.len()` was thrown away.

Measured in release: 1.66 ms/frame at 192x80 (0.41 ms at 100x40) — at the 30fps
tick that is ~50 ms of CPU per second of runtime, spent on a value that only
changes when the terminal is resized.

The sweep is a pure function of (buf_w, buf_h, desk_cap) and publishes through
a monotone `fetch_max`, so a repeat with identical inputs could only rewrite
the same numbers. `FloorCapacitySweep` memoizes on exactly that key: 1.66 ms
-> 0.000002 ms on a steady frame, unchanged work on a resize.

Factored out of the codecov-excluded loop so the memo and the published values
are unit-testable, mirroring `toggle_intent` / `dispatch_key`.

fix(ci): close the fork-tree exposure and the silent review gate (#822)

* fix(ci): refuse fork pull requests in the contents:write Claude job

The two `pull_request_review*` arms were hardened in #794 against a fork
tree arriving via GITHUB_REF. `issue_comment` reaches the same state by a
route no `if:` can express: its payload carries no `pull_request` object,
and claude-code-action stages the head itself — tag mode's `setupBranch`
runs `git checkout` for every open PR, with the fork/non-fork split
affecting only how the ref is fetched (verified against the pinned v1
source; no input disables it, and `allowed_non_write_users` governs who
may trigger, not what is checked out).

So a maintainer typing `@claude` on a fork PR staged fork-authored files —
a repo-root CLAUDE.md the agent auto-loads as instructions among them — in
the one job holding contents:write and the OAuth token. The existing
author_association gate does not help: the trusted maintainer IS the
trigger in that scenario.

Closing it costs less than the issue assumed. Both other Claude paths
already refuse forks (the automatic arm by `if:`, the reusable workflow at
its resolve step), so fork PRs had no Claude coverage to lose — the
`@claude` arm was the only one still reaching them, by doing the unsafe
thing.

The policy rule keys on the API field the step must READ rather than its
name, and pins that it precedes the action: a refusal running after the
tree is staged is decoration. Verified against real data — PR #818
(same-repo) passes, PR #726 (a real fork) is refused, and a deleted fork
resolves to "" and fails closed.

* fix(ci): say when the review did not run, instead of looking clean

The merge gate is "the review bot's `Findings: 0` at HEAD". When the model
job fails, `publish` is gated on its outcome and SKIPS, so no comment lands
at HEAD, and with `ci-gate` the only required check the PR reads UNSTABLE —
indistinguishable from a flaky advisory. That is how #805-#818 merged with
the second lens absent: the condition was noticed, but its cause was
misread twice.

A spent quota is an operating condition, not an incident, so this will
recur. A third job now states the absence at HEAD.

It keys off `needs.analyze.result` and `inputs.pr_number`, never the failed
job's `outputs` — GitHub does not document output propagation from a failed
job, and a reporter that silently stops running is the exact failure mode
it exists to prevent.

Also surface why: the action reports a rejected request as
`subtype: "success"` with a missing structured_output, so its error blames
the JSON schema whatever the cause. The `result` object separates them —
a rejected request spends $0 in 1 turn; a real run spent $1.05 over 24
turns. Those fields now reach the job summary.

fix(grok): route active_sessions pids through checked_pid so one bad entry skips (#840)

grok's registry probe deserialized entries into `pid: i32` and hand-rolled
`e.pid <= 0`, bypassing the shared `decoder::checked_pid`. A pid outside i32
range therefore failed `serde_json::from_slice` for the WHOLE document ->
`.ok()?` -> None -> a `shape_drift` breadcrumb claiming the registry's shape
changed upstream -> all grok liveness degraded to mtime. CC's registry skips the
offending entry and keeps its siblings; grok now does too.

Not a validation hole: grok already rejected non-positive pids twice over. What
this buys is (a) `checked_pid`'s completeness claim becomes true — that doc is
what the next pid ingress reads to decide whether it is covered — and (b) a
false upstream-drift breadcrumb goes away. Upstream types the field `u32` and
pid_max is 2^22, so the value is not reachable from a real grok build.

The i64 widening makes the downstream fan-out compiler-enforced at 3 of its 4
use sites (`tracing::debug!` impls Value for both widths, so that one is not).

Tests: an out-of-range pid skips only its own entry, asserted in both orders
with a no-truncation check (4294967297 as i32 == 1); the junk-values case grows
a negative pid and a live sibling; and a negative control pins that a mistyped
or renamed pid key is still document-level drift — the derive's strictness IS
the #247 rename detector, and a mutation matrix confirmed it is the only test
that kills a `Vec<Value>` refactor.

refactor(grok): delete the inert #638 leader vouch rather than repair it (#851)

The vouch never fired on any platform: `leader_socket_owner` asked
`fd_probe::open_vnode_paths` whether a pid holds `leader.sock` open, and that fn
reports VNODE descriptors only — a unix socket is not one (macOS
PROX_FDTYPE_SOCKET; Linux /proc/<pid>/fd/N resolves to the non-path
socket:[inode]).

Repairing the probe was adjudicated against, twice over. It was the SECOND
defect: augment_with_fresh_sessions bound the leader with or_insert, so the
registry's CLIENT pid still won — and that is the pid ProbeLadder::fold hands
the ExitWatch, so the client's death ended the session in milliseconds while the
leader binding could only migrate in on the 60s poll. And the vouch was
mtime-derived, so it expired while the session was still alive; an id leaving a
HEALTHY snapshot is exactly the negative-vouch trigger (~240s) where the
unvouched session survives to the 300s short-idle reap. The lever was
arithmetically zero (150 + 150 = 300), and a firing vouch re-admitted the parked
transcript at cursor 0 — full replay plus a phantom SessionStart.

A working replacement was built and four-lens reviewed before being set aside:
it fixed the symptom but left four residuals and two design issues, because it
inferred ownership from a registry that does not model it.

Session-to-leader ownership lives only in leader/server.rs's in-memory
session_driver/session_subscribers maps. active_sessions.json gives the client
pid; leader{suffix}.lock gives the leader's pid and liveness but not which
sessions; the transcripts carry no ownership signal because the writer opens and
drops the fd per append (session/storage/jsonl/mod.rs::append_jsonl_line_sync_with,
verified upstream — so no Codex-style open-fd probe is possible); and the control
protocol's nine ControlCommand variants include no list-sessions. Every in-tree
fix is therefore a proxy with its own failure mode, which is what #638 was. The
real fix is upstream exposing the fact — tracked in #839.

No user-visible change: leader sessions keep the pre-#638 path (mtime gate +
short-idle reap + prompt resurrect), which is what they have done for the
feature's entire shipped life.

Pinned by a differential oracle — the same tree read twice, once with a real
bound and listening UnixListener at the leader path — proven RED before the
deletion by reintroducing a firing vouch.

Part of #826.

fix(grok): stop breadcrumbing task_complete as unknown notification drift (#842)

Upstream dispatches a notification hook with notification_type "task_complete" on
every background-task completion (xai-grok-shell/src/tools/notification_bridge.rs,
which asserts that exact string in five of its own tests). Our notification arm
matched only permission_prompt / elicitation_dialog / idle_prompt / agent_error,
so it fell to the `other` arm and fired drift::unknown_event — undeduped on the
hook plane by design, so routine background work reported as a recurring "the
wire changed" warning across pixtuoid doctor, the footer drift nudge, and the

Bash|Monitor, never a subagent, with no toolUseId — and the spawning tool call
already Ended at BACKGROUNDING time (the same fires-at-spawn fact grok's b1 trap
turns on), so there is nothing to close.

The old test could not have caught this: a knowingly-ignored type and an
unrecognized one both decode to zero events. The new test separates them on the
breadcrumb, with a novel type as a live control so the silence assertions are
recognition rather than a dead detector. It strictly subsumes the old one, which
is deleted — removing one of the five copies of this vocabulary.

Two drift items were deliberately excluded after failing verification, and the
reasoning is recorded so neither is re-proposed: a drift-watch row for the
notificationType VALUE vocabulary (upstream types the field as a bare String and
mints the values at scattered dispatch sites, so no declaration owns them — the
#793 anchor-grade lesson; now a sharp edge as defense-#2-only, the antigravity
class), and a verified_version bump (that field means "decoder AND fixtures, by

verification nobody performed).

fix(focus): close both Windows focus-jump gaps (#882)

Windows focus-jump was a double no-op: shim-family sources sent no pid at all,
and the one activation call the binary made is the one the system refuses.

- **pid channel** — the shim walks one Toolhelp32 snapshot past the transient
  `cmd /C` parent instead of trusting getppid (`pixtuoid-hook/src/cli_pid.rs`).
  The walk gets its own budget on a worker thread so a snapshot an AV/EDR filter
  slows cannot eat the send's: losing `_pid` costs a focus jump, losing the
  envelope costs the sprite. Resolution is lazy — a plugin that stamped its own
  `process.pid` never pays for a walk.
- **recycle guard** — `pid_start_marker` grows a Windows arm (creation FILETIME
  via GetProcessTimes), which is what makes shipping the pid safe: #527's
  click-time check is live there rather than inert.
- **foreground lock** — `activate_os` tries unattached first (all the `floating`
  painter needs), then retries under an RAII AttachThreadInput borrow. The
  PeekMessage prime is load-bearing: without a message queue the attach fails
  outright, and a console TUI is exactly the thread that may not have one.

Refused deliberately, recorded as a sharp edge: the SendInput ALT tap (injects a
global input event into whatever app the user is typing in) and FreeConsole
(would detach the console the TUI draws into).

Verified: `windows-test` executes the FFI, the marker, and a real `cmd /C` walk
asserting the grandparent's pid. The activation itself is unreachable headlessly
— the macOS live dogfood is widened to Windows for a human.

fix(tooling): stop gen-guides' selftest from staging into the real index (#888)

`git -C <dir>` does NOT outrank an inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` — git's
env wins. `scripts/gen-guides.py --selftest` builds a throwaway repo and runs
`git -C <tmp> add -A` against it, so whenever the script runs with those vars
exported the staging lands in the REAL index instead.

That is not hypothetical: `just lint` runs the selftest, and the pre-push hook
runs `just lint`, so every `git push` did it. The observed damage was the outer
index dropping from 798 tracked files to 4, holding one phantom
`crate/CLAUDE.md` — the selftest fixture's path, staged into the wrong repo.

It also PERSISTS. Nothing re-reads the tree afterwards, so the next
`gen-guides.py --check` asks `git ls-files '*CLAUDE.md'`, gets the phantom back,
and dies on a path that was never on disk:

    FileNotFoundError: .../crate/CLAUDE.md

which reads as a broken guide index rather than a broken index file, and
survives every later command until someone runs `git read-tree HEAD` by hand.
CI never saw it — no hooks there — so this only ever bit locally, at push time,
and looked like the guides gate had spontaneously failed.

Nothing in this script wants an ambient git context: every call already passes
`-C`. So `drop_ambient_git_env()` clears `GIT_*` once at the entry point.

Pinned by an 11th negative control, run LAST so a leak cannot corrupt the
fixture above it: an `outer` repo stands in for the developer's checkout, its
`ls-files` is captured, `GIT_DIR` is pointed at it, and a throwaway `git add`
runs in a THIRD directory. The outer index must be byte-identical afterwards.
Removing the scrub reds it with the symptom named — `it now holds
['PHANTOM.md']` — rather than a bare boolean.

* refactor(fixtures): record the shim's OUTPUT, which is the seam every source shares

The recorder teed the shim's STDIN, which cannot cover every source: codewhale is
env-mode — identity arrives in `DEEPSEEK_*` vars and the shim never touches stdin
when `--event` is present, precisely so a hook child cannot block the TUI on an
inherited terminal — so a stdin tee captures a file of empty payloads. That is
why codewhale was written down as permanently unrecordable. It is not; the
recorder was listening on the wrong side.

`PIXTUOID_SOCKET` is the seam. It is an explicit override the shim honors ahead
of everything (`paths::default_socket_path`) and deliberately exempts from the
peer-uid check that guards the owned-tmp fallback, so a listener of our own
receives exactly the line production's reducer would. Recording there does not
care how the payload reached the shim.

Three things fall out, all simplifications:

- **The CLI's installed config is never touched.** No `PIXTUOID_HOOK` override,
  no `connect`, no restore, and no `$XDG_STATE_HOME` marker for the `kill -9`
  that skips the EXIT trap — all of it deleted. The hook the CLI already has is
  the one that runs, which also makes the capture an install check: a
  DISCONNECTED source is refused before the turn is spent, not after.
- **Tearing is structural, not defended against.** `transport::send_line`
  connects, writes one line, closes, so one accept IS one whole payload. The
  atomic-mkdir slot claim is gone with the tee that needed it.
- **Nothing edits the bytes.** The shim stamps `_pixtuoid_source` itself now that
  we read downstream of it, so the allowed hand edits drop from two to one:
  redact PII.

Captures from this seam carry production's `_shim_ts_ms` / `_pid`, which fixtures
older than it do not — noted in the README rather than stripped, since stripping
would be an edit and the stamps are frozen once committed.

payloads (the case the old recorder was blind to) with `cwd`/`tool`/`tool_args`

* fix(hook): cursor re-delivers every event, and each copy counted as a tool call

Measured, not inferred. A counting wrapper on the shim — no recorder anywhere in
the loop — logged 24 hook invocations for a single one-tool `cursor-agent -p`
turn, roughly 4-6 per event, each from its OWN shell parent. The control was
free and independent: an unrelated debug-tee hook registered on the same events
in the same run logged each exactly once, and a socket-side capture matched the
wrapper count exactly (37 = 37), which is what cleared the recorder of causing it.

The damage is `apply_activity_start`, which increments `tool_call_count`
unconditionally (reducer/mod.rs:486). cursor's decoder drops `tool_use_id` by
design, so nothing downstream could tell the copies apart and a cursor session's
tool count in the HUD ran several times the truth.

`hook::dedup` drops a re-delivery at the socket, before decode. **The gate, not
the window, is what makes it safe**: only a payload carrying its source's own
per-call id takes part, and two genuine calls of the same tool on the same file
carry DIFFERENT ids — so the collision the fix must never make cannot happen.
Id-less payloads (session lifecycle, codewhale's `event`+`cwd` envelope) pass
straight through and are idempotent in the reducer anyway. The id's spelling
comes from the `ToolIdKey` registry row this branch added for kimi, so kimi's
`tool_call_id` gates it too without a second copy of the name.

The fingerprint is the whole payload minus the shim's `_shim_ts_ms`/`_pid`, which
is why a Pre and its Post do not collide despite sharing an id — no event-field
name is hardcoded anywhere. Bounded by count (256), not a clock: a per-call id
names one call, so a repeat is a duplicate whenever it lands, and the bound needs
no time source to test.

Seven unit tests plus one through `handle_conn` itself, since the unit tests
cannot prove the wiring. Negative-controlled: short-circuiting the gate makes the
`handle_conn` test report 3 ActivityStarts where it demands 2.

chore(ci): CodeQL drops rust/cleartext-logging — every hit is a test assert (#975)

The query is a name heuristic (`maybeAccountInfo` in shared/concepts/codeql/concepts/internal/SensitiveDataHeuristics.qll) that reads every `*_session_id` as a credential. Here a session id is an agent CLI's local key, hashed into `AgentId` at the decode boundary, and every alert the rule has raised (47: 35 open, 11 dismissed "used in tests", 1 fixed) is a test's failure message echoing one — 32 inside `#[cfg(test)]` modules, 3 under `tests/`. Dismissals are per-location, so each new test file re-raised the class.

The exclusion rides an inline `config:` on the init step (a documented input; a separate config file would be invisible to the Rego policy's document set). `CARGO_ALL_TARGETS` is policy-pinned and `paths-ignore` is file-level, so per-query is the narrowest mechanism CodeQL offers.

What the filter forgoes: the query's sinks are prints and panics (the `log-injection` rows in rust/ql/lib/codeql/rust/frameworks/log.model.yml), never `tracing`, which CodeQL does not model. Being repo-wide it also forgoes the heuristic's password / secret / certificate name classes at print sinks; today no production crate holds such a value. Removing the filter, or an upstream id rename, returns the alerts in the Security tab after the next main scan (a PR's CodeQL check counts only alerts in changed code); a Rego pin is the owner's call as its own PR.

Positive control: the PR-ref Rust analysis reports 24 rules / 0 results against main's 25 / 36; the other three languages are unchanged. Two-lens review: three lenses round 1 (one MEDIUM — the WHY's sink claim — fixed), round-2 delta verify CONVERGED; bots: auto-review 0 findings, security-review 1 medium (the accepted cost above).

* ci(release): release-plz derives the bump and tags a merged release PR

The only judgement left in the release flow was the bump level, picked by
hand in `just bump` and upheld "in review". release-plz derives it from
the conventional-commit log plus cargo-semver-checks, so the human steps
become: dispatch, regenerate the committed art on the PR, merge.

release-plz owns versions and the tag ONLY; release.yml is untouched and
still owns every irreversible publish (crates.io + npm over OIDC, the
GitHub release, provenance). `publish = false` keeps it that way, and
`git_tag_name = "v{{ version }}"` is what release.yml's `v*` trigger and
homebrew-core's autobump need — release-plz's multi-package default
(`{{ package }}-v{{ version }}`) would match neither.

`semver_check = false`: the step holding the PAT must run no compiler,
or every dependency's build script runs with a write credential in its
environment. ci-builds' `semver` job answers the same question on the
release PR instead, guarded per STEP because require-jobs reds a skipped
job. That is also where the per-PR gate went: between releases main
carries unreleased changes at the shipped version, where a baseline
check reds by design.

`release-pr` is dispatch-only. release-plz refreshes an open release PR
on every push to main, closing and re-opening one that carries non-bot
commits — which would orphan the human's regenerated stills on the next
dependabot merge.

Two silent failures get mechanisms, both being classes that reach green:
- a tag created with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow, so `release.yml`
  would never fire. Policy pins both release-plz steps to a repository
  secret (never the automatic token), by the effective step<job<workflow
  env the zizmor token rule already resolves, generalised over the name.
- release-plz tags only a merged `release-plz-*` branch and DECLINES
  silently otherwise. The `tag` job asserts main's workspace version is
  tagged — true at rest on every push, false exactly when a bump landed
  untagged.

The six policy rules pin what is otherwise invisible: two live action
steps carrying the exact `{release-pr, release}` command set (the action
runs BOTH when `command:` is absent, so a step that loses the input
opens a release PR on every push while the count still reads two), each
`[workspace]` kill switch with the reason true for IT, exactly one
tagging package, and the two cross-file pairs a one-sided edit breaks —
`git_tag_name` against release.yml's tag glob, `pr_name` (the squash
subject) against cliff.toml's skip parser. `release-plz.toml` and
`cliff.toml` join the conftest document set; yq fixes its input format
per call, so the TOML pair rides a second call joined with jq.

`pr_branch_prefix` is declared rather than inherited: it is release-plz's
own default, and three of our mechanisms key on that literal.

Needs the RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN secret (fine-grained PAT, this repository,
Contents + Pull requests read/write) BEFORE this reaches main — the
`tag` job runs on every push and the action refuses an empty token.

* fix(release): the changelog covers the whole workspace, not just the first crate

The v0.19.0 release PR's CHANGELOG.md held 12 entries — every one a commit
touching `pixtuoid-core`. The board revamp (#1009), the version popup's move to
GitHub release notes (#1006) and everything else in scene/bin were absent, and
that file is the draft release's body: the very notes the popup now sends users
to.

Cause: `changelog_path = "./CHANGELOG.md"` sat at WORKSPACE level, so all four
packages wrote the same `## [0.19.0]` heading to one file; the first writer won
and the PR body showed four identical sections. release-plz's documented lever
is `changelog_include` ("include commits that belong to other packages"), and
its own release-plz.toml (fetched) uses exactly this shape: the released package
owns the root changelog and names the rest. Workspace `changelog_update = false`
keeps the other crates from writing per-crate files.

Verified with `release-plz update` 0.3.169 on a throwaway worktree of main:
12 -> 19 entries, incl. #1009 tagged **breaking**, #1006, #1010, #1007; no
per-crate CHANGELOG.md appears. Commits touching no workspace member (site/, ci)
stay out by design.

Pinned, because the failure is silent: `changelog_update` joins the workspace
kill-switches, and the package that carries the draft release must write the
changelog AND name every other member of Cargo.toml's `[workspace].members` —
Cargo.toml becomes a policy input. Checked against the real files: dropping
`pixtuoid-web` from the list reds `just ci-observability` by name.
